name: duckhts_simd_backend
description: Return the current DuckHTS SIMD dispatch label. For explicit scalar or concrete backend requests this is the requested policy; for auto it is the single selected backend when all logical kernels resolve to the same backend, or mixed when per-kernel auto-dispatch resolves to multiple backends. Use duckhts_simd_kernel_info() for per-kernel details.

name: duckhts_simd_requested_backend
description: Return the current explicit SIMD backend request, usually auto unless `SELECT backend FROM duckhts_simd_set_backend('auto'|'scalar'|backend)` was called. The selected per-kernel backend may differ under auto-dispatch across x86, ARM, wasm, and scalar-only builds.

name: duckhts_simd_backend_compiled
description: Return whether a concrete DuckHTS SIMD backend was compiled into this build. This is independent of whether the current CPU/runtime supports executing that backend; for example avx512 can be compiled but not CPU-supported on the running host.

name: duckhts_simd_backend_cpu_supported
description: Return whether the current CPU/runtime supports a concrete DuckHTS SIMD backend, independent of whether DuckHTS compiled an implementation for it. Availability is the intersection of compiled and CPU-supported.

name: duckhts_simd_backend_available
description: Return whether a concrete SIMD backend is usable in the current process. Availability means the backend is compiled into DuckHTS and supported by the current CPU/runtime. auto is a selection request rather than a concrete backend and is not reported as available here.
examples: SELECT duckhts_simd_backend_available('scalar'); || SELECT duckhts_simd_backend_available('avx2'); || SELECT duckhts_simd_backend_available('avx512');

name: duckhts_simd_info
description: Return one row per known concrete DuckHTS SIMD backend with extension-owned selectable, compiled, CPU-supported, available, selected, requested, and dispatch-mode diagnostics. Availability is the intersection of compiled and CPU/runtime-supported. selectable reports whether the backend has a selectable implementation path; explicit selection still requires available = TRUE. selected is TRUE when the current dispatch table uses that backend for at least one logical kernel. auto is a selection request and is not a concrete backend row.
examples: SELECT * FROM duckhts_simd_info(); || SELECT backend FROM duckhts_simd_info() WHERE available;

name: duckhts_simd_kernel_info
description: Return one row per logical DuckHTS SIMD kernel showing the concrete backend selected by the current immutable dispatch table, the selected capability, the requested backend policy, whether scalar was used as a per-kernel fallback, and the dispatch mode. This is the authoritative diagnostic for mixed auto-dispatch when different kernels resolve to different backends.
examples: SELECT * FROM duckhts_simd_kernel_info(); || SELECT kernel, selected_backend FROM duckhts_simd_kernel_info();

name: duckhts_simd_set_backend
description: Explicitly select the DuckHTS SIMD dispatch policy for this process using a one-row table-function call and return the current dispatch label in a backend column. Use auto for per-kernel runtime dispatch or scalar for a portable baseline; unavailable platform-specific requests such as avx512 on non-AVX-512 CPUs raise an error instead of silently falling back.
examples: SELECT backend FROM duckhts_simd_set_backend('scalar'); || SELECT backend FROM duckhts_simd_set_backend('auto');

name: read_bcf
signature: read_bcf(path, region := NULL, index_path := NULL, tidy_format := FALSE, additional_csq_column_types := NULL, decompression_threads := 0)
description: Read VCF and BCF variant data with typed INFO, FORMAT, typed CSQ/ANN/BCSQ subfields, optional tidy sample output, optional bcftools-style CSQ type overrides, and optional htslib decompression worker threads via decompression_threads (default 0 for single-threaded reads).
examples: SELECT CHROM, POS, REF, ALT FROM read_bcf('vcf_file.bcf') LIMIT 5;

name: read_bam
signature: read_bam(path, standard_tags := FALSE, auxiliary_tags := FALSE, region := NULL, index_path := NULL, reference := NULL, sequence_encoding := 'string', quality_representation := 'string', cigar_representation := 'string', decompression_threads := 2)
description: Read SAM, BAM, and CRAM alignments with optional typed SAMtags and auxiliary tag maps. Use sequence_encoding := 'nt16' to return SEQ as UTINYINT[], quality_representation := 'phred' to return QUAL as UTINYINT[], and cigar_representation := 'binary' to return packed BAM CIGAR operations as UINTEGER[] instead of SAM text. decompression_threads controls per-file htslib worker threads and defaults to 2; use 0 to disable worker threads.
examples: SELECT QNAME, FLAG, RNAME, POS FROM read_bam('range.bam') LIMIT 5;

name: read_pileup
signature: read_pileup(path, region := NULL, index_path := NULL, min_mapq := 0, flag_mask := 1796)
description: Construct a region-scoped BAM pileup with one row per covered position, emitting chrom, 1-based position, depth, observed bases, and Phred+33 qualities after SAM flag and MAPQ filtering. This is a compact htslib pileup view, not samtools mpileup text parity.
examples: SELECT chrom, pos, depth FROM read_pileup('range.bam', region := 'CHROMOSOME_I:1-200') LIMIT 5;

name: read_fasta
signature: read_fasta(path, region := NULL, index_path := NULL, gzi_path := NULL, sequence_encoding := 'string')
description: Read FASTA records or indexed FASTA regions as sequence rows. Use sequence_encoding := 'nt16' to return SEQUENCE as UTINYINT[] (htslib nt16 4-bit codes) instead of VARCHAR. For bgzipped FASTA, gzi_path may point to an explicit .gzi sidecar when it is not colocated with the FASTA.

name: read_bed
description: Read BED3-BED12 interval files with canonical typed columns and optional tabix-backed region filtering.
examples: SELECT chrom, start, "end", name FROM read_bed('targets.bed') LIMIT 5;

name: fasta_nuc
signature: fasta_nuc(path, bed_path := NULL, bin_width := NULL, region := NULL, index_path := NULL, gzi_path := NULL, bed_index_path := NULL, include_seq := FALSE)
description: Compute bedtools nuc-style nucleotide composition for supplied BED intervals or generated fixed-width bins over a FASTA reference. For bgzipped FASTA, gzi_path may point to an explicit .gzi sidecar when it is not colocated with the FASTA.
examples: SELECT chrom, start, "end", pct_gc FROM fasta_nuc('ce.fa', bin_width := 1000) LIMIT 5;

name: duckhts_cgranges_create
description: Create an empty session-scoped cgranges registry entry that can be populated with intervals and finalized for overlap queries.

name: duckhts_cgranges_add
description: Append an interval to a session-scoped cgranges registry entry before finalization. Labels may be BIGINT-like, DOUBLE, VARCHAR, or BOOLEAN.

name: duckhts_cgranges_index
description: Finalize a populated cgranges registry entry and build its immutable overlap index for subsequent queries.

name: duckhts_cgranges_destroy
description: Destroy a session-scoped cgranges registry entry and release its indexed interval storage when it is not in active use.

name: duckhts_cgranges_from_query
signature: duckhts_cgranges_from_query(name, query, chrom_col, start_col, end_col[, label_col])
description: Execute a SQL query on an extension-owned DuckDB connection, append its interval rows into a session-scoped cgranges registry entry, and leave the populated index ready for explicit finalization with duckhts_cgranges_index(...).
examples: SELECT duckhts_cgranges_from_query('targets_idx', 'SELECT chrom, start, "end", name FROM targets', 'chrom', 'start', 'end', 'name');

name: duckhts_cgranges_from_table
signature: duckhts_cgranges_from_table(name, table_name, chrom_col, start_col, end_col[, label_col])
description: Reserved convenience constructor for bulk cgranges population from a table name. The current implementation is intentionally deferred and directs callers to duckhts_cgranges_from_query(...).

name: duckhts_cgranges_has_overlap
description: Vectorized scalar predicate for streaming provider rows through a finalized session-scoped cgranges index. Returns TRUE when the query interval overlaps at least one indexed interval, or when mode = 'contain' and it fully contains at least one indexed interval; NULL inputs return NULL.
examples: SELECT * FROM read_bed('queries.bed') WHERE duckhts_cgranges_has_overlap('targets_idx', chrom, start, "end");

name: duckhts_cgranges_count_overlaps
description: Vectorized scalar overlap counter for streaming provider rows through a finalized session-scoped cgranges index. Returns the number of indexed intervals that overlap the query interval, or with mode = 'contain' the number fully contained by it; NULL inputs return NULL.
examples: SELECT chrom, start, "end", duckhts_cgranges_count_overlaps('targets_idx', chrom, start, "end") AS n_targets FROM read_bed('queries.bed');

name: duckhts_cgranges_overlaps_list
returns: STRUCT(interval_ordinal BIGINT, label VARCHAR, label_type VARCHAR, interval_chrom VARCHAR, interval_start INTEGER, interval_end INTEGER)[]
description: Vectorized scalar overlap expander for streaming provider rows through a finalized session-scoped cgranges index. Returns a LIST of hit STRUCTs that can be expanded with UNNEST, preserving provider columns while emitting one row per matching indexed interval. Because scalar return types are fixed, labels are returned as text with label_type describing the original cgranges label kind; NULL inputs return NULL.
examples: SELECT q.*, hit.interval_chrom, hit.interval_start, hit.interval_end, hit.label FROM read_bed('queries.bed') AS q CROSS JOIN UNNEST(duckhts_cgranges_overlaps_list('targets_idx', q.chrom, q.start, q."end")) AS u(hit);

name: duckhts_cgranges_overlaps
signature: duckhts_cgranges_overlaps(name, chrom, start, end, mode := 'overlap', query_row_id := NULL)
description: Query a finalized session-scoped cgranges registry entry and return one row per overlapping or containing indexed interval, preserving the original label type and interval coordinates.

name: duckhts_cgranges_overlaps_bulk
signature: duckhts_cgranges_overlaps_bulk(name, query, chrom_col, start_col, end_col, mode := 'overlap', query_row_id_col := NULL)
description: Run a SQL query that yields overlap probes, stream those rows through a finalized session-scoped cgranges registry entry, and return one row per matching indexed interval. The probe query runs on the extension-owned helper connection, so it must reference regular tables/views rather than connection-local temp tables. When query_row_id_col is omitted, query_row_id defaults to the 1-based probe row ordinal.
examples: SELECT * FROM duckhts_cgranges_overlaps_bulk('targets_idx', 'SELECT probe_id, chrom, start, "end" FROM probes', 'chrom', 'start', 'end', query_row_id_col := 'probe_id');

name: read_fastq
signature: read_fastq(path, interleaved := FALSE, mate_path := NULL, sequence_encoding := 'string', quality_representation := 'string', input_quality_encoding := 'phred33')
description: Read single-end, paired-end, or interleaved FASTQ files with optional legacy quality decoding. By default, FASTQ qualities are interpreted as modern Phred+33 input. Use sequence_encoding := 'nt16' to return SEQUENCE as UTINYINT[] and quality_representation := 'phred' to return QUALITY as UTINYINT[] instead of VARCHAR. input_quality_encoding accepts 'phred33', 'auto', 'phred64', or 'solexa64'.
examples: SELECT NAME, MATE FROM read_fastq('r1.fq', mate_path := 'r2.fq') LIMIT 5;

name: detect_quality_encoding
description: Inspect a FASTQ file's observed quality ASCII range and report compatible legacy encodings with a heuristic guessed encoding.

name: read_gff
signature: read_gff(path, header_names := NULL, header := FALSE, column_types := NULL, auto_detect := FALSE, attributes_map := FALSE, attributes_list := FALSE, attributes_pairs := FALSE, strict := FALSE, region := NULL, index_path := NULL)
description: Read GFF annotations with optional raw scalar and richer list/pair parsed attribute columns, strict GFF3 structural validation, and indexed region filtering.
examples: SELECT seqname, feature, start, "end" FROM read_gff('gff_file.gff.gz') LIMIT 5;

name: read_gtf
signature: read_gtf(path, header_names := NULL, header := FALSE, column_types := NULL, auto_detect := FALSE, attributes_map := FALSE, attributes_list := FALSE, attributes_pairs := FALSE, region := NULL, index_path := NULL)
description: Read GTF annotations with optional raw scalar and richer list/pair parsed attribute columns and indexed region filtering.
examples: SELECT seqname, feature, start, "end" FROM read_gtf('annotations.gtf.gz') LIMIT 5;

name: read_tabix
signature: read_tabix(path, header_names := NULL, header := FALSE, column_types := NULL, auto_detect := FALSE, region := NULL, index_path := NULL)
description: Read generic tabix-indexed text data with optional header handling and type inference.

name: fasta_index
description: Build a FASTA index (.fai) and return a single row with columns success (BOOLEAN) and index_path (VARCHAR).

name: bgzip
signature: bgzip(path, output_path := NULL, threads := 4, level := -1, keep := TRUE, overwrite := FALSE)
description: Compress a plain file to BGZF and return the created output path and byte counts.

name: bgunzip
signature: bgunzip(path, output_path := NULL, threads := 4, keep := TRUE, overwrite := FALSE)
description: Decompress a BGZF-compressed file and return the created output path and byte counts.

name: bam_index
description: Build a BAM or CRAM index and report the written index path and format.

name: bcf_index
signature: bcf_index(path, index_path := NULL, min_shift := NULL, threads := 4)
description: Build a TBI or CSI index for a VCF or BCF file and report the written index path and format.

name: tabix_index
signature: tabix_index(path, preset := 'vcf', index_path := NULL, min_shift := 0, threads := 4, seq_col := NULL, start_col := NULL, end_col := NULL, comment_char := NULL, skip_lines := NULL)
description: Build a tabix index for a BGZF-compressed text file using a preset or explicit coordinate columns.

name: bam_bin_counts
signature: bam_bin_counts(path, bin_width, chrom := NULL, reference := NULL, index_path := NULL, mapq := 0, require_flags := 0, exclude_flags := 0, rmdup := 'none', stats := NULL)
description: Count BAM or CRAM read starts into fixed-width bins. Returns one row per bin across the selected contig span, including zero-count bins, with total, forward, and reverse counts; `rmdup := 'streaming'` applies the WisecondorX-style larp/larp2 consecutive-position deduplication, `rmdup := 'flag'` drops SAM duplicate-flagged reads, and `stats := 'gc'`, `'mq'`, or `'gc,mq'` adds per-bin pre/post-filter GC and MAPQ sufficient statistics, including reference GC when `reference` is provided.
examples: SELECT * FROM bam_bin_counts('fixture_mixed.cram', 5000, reference := 'fixture_ref.fa', rmdup := 'streaming', stats := 'gc,mq');

name: duckhts_bam_bed_coverage
signature: duckhts_bam_bed_coverage(path, bed_path, reference := NULL, index_path := NULL, bed_index_path := NULL, mapq := 0, min_baseq := 0, min_read_len := 0, require_flags := 0, exclude_flags := 1796, min_depth := 1, max_depth := 1000000, decompression_threads := 0, fragment_mode := FALSE, strand_outputs := TRUE, processing_threads := 0)
description: Compute samtools coverage-like regional summaries for BAM or CRAM input over a BED target set, returning one row per BED interval with DuckHTS-specific pre/post-filter read counts, covered bases, percentage covered, mean depth, mean baseQ, mean mapQ, and strand-specific post-filter summaries in read mode. Indexed BAM/CRAM input is required in the current implementation. decompression_threads controls htslib worker threads for BAM/CRAM decoding; use 0 to disable them.
examples: SELECT chrom, start, "end", numreads_post, covbases_post, coverage_post FROM duckhts_bam_bed_coverage('fixture_mixed.bam', 'fixture_mixed_regions.bed');

name: duckhts_mosdepth
signature: duckhts_mosdepth(prefix, path, chrom := NULL, by := NULL, fasta := NULL, read_groups := NULL, no_per_base := FALSE, threads := 2, processing_threads := 2, flag := 1796, include_flag := 0, fast_mode := FALSE, fragment_mode := FALSE, use_median := FALSE, mapq := 0, min_frag_len := -1, max_frag_len := -1, precision_digits := 2, quantize := NULL, thresholds := NULL, index_path := NULL, overwrite := FALSE)
description: Write native mosdepth-compatible coverage outputs for indexed BAM or CRAM input. Produces mosdepth-style summary, global distribution, per-base BED.gz + CSI, optional window/BED region outputs, optional quantized BED.gz + CSI, and optional threshold counts for `by`; `fast_mode` defaults to FALSE to match upstream mosdepth, default mode performs CIGAR-aware coverage with mate-overlap correction, `fragment_mode` switches coverage to full-fragment insert spans for proper pairs, `use_median` switches `by` outputs from mean to median, `read_groups` filters by comma-separated RG IDs, `min_frag_len` and `max_frag_len` filter on absolute template length, `fasta` is required for CRAM when htslib needs a reference, `precision_digits` controls decimal places in the text outputs, and `processing_threads` enables parallel contig processing (0 = sequential, >0 = number of worker threads).
examples: SELECT * FROM duckhts_mosdepth('sample', 'range.cram', fasta := 'ce.fa', by := '1000', fragment_mode := TRUE, read_groups := '1', use_median := TRUE, min_frag_len := 50, max_frag_len := 500, quantize := ':1:4:', thresholds := '1,10,20', precision_digits := 4, overwrite := TRUE);

name: duckhts_samtools_idxstats
signature: duckhts_samtools_idxstats(path, output := NULL, index_path := NULL, threads := 0, overwrite := FALSE)
description: Write samtools idxstats-compatible TAB-delimited output for BAM, CRAM, or SAM input. Indexed BAM uses `hts_idx_get_stat(...)` for the fast path; CRAM, SAM, and unindexed BAM fall back to a full scan while preserving samtools-style contig rows plus the final `*` row.
examples: SELECT * FROM duckhts_samtools_idxstats('range.bam', output := 'range.idxstats.txt', overwrite := TRUE);

name: read_hts_header
description: Inspect HTS headers in parsed, raw, or combined form across supported formats.
examples: SELECT record_type, id FROM read_hts_header('formatcols.vcf.gz') LIMIT 10;

name: read_hts_index
description: Inspect high-level HTS index metadata such as sequence names and mapped counts.

name: read_hts_index_spans
description: Expand index metadata into span and chunk rows suitable for low-level index inspection.
examples: SELECT seqname, chunk_beg_vo, chunk_end_vo FROM read_hts_index_spans('vcf_file.bcf') LIMIT 5;

name: read_hts_index_raw
description: Return the raw on-disk HTS index blob together with basic identifying metadata.

name: variantkey
description: Encode a normalized biallelic variant as an official VariantKey-compatible 64-bit unsigned integer. This DuckHTS wrapper accepts 1-based VCF/DuckHTS POS to match bcftools `%VKX` / `+add-variantkey`, internally converts to the upstream 0-based field, and preserves the official hashed nonreversible mode for large, ambiguous, and symbolic REF/ALT strings. Only CHROM, POS, REF, and ALT are encoded; END, SVLEN, mate breakend coordinates, and other SV metadata are not.

name: variantkey_hex
description: Render a VariantKey as its lowercase 16-character hexadecimal string representation.

name: parse_variantkey_hex
description: Parse a 16-character hexadecimal VariantKey string back into its UBIGINT code. Invalid or non-hex strings return NULL.

name: encode_variantkey
description: Encode the raw upstream VariantKey fields directly: chromosome code, 0-based position, and 31-bit REF+ALT code.

name: extract_variantkey_chrom
description: Extract the raw upstream VariantKey chromosome code.

name: extract_variantkey_pos
description: Extract the raw upstream VariantKey 0-based position field.

name: extract_variantkey_refalt
description: Extract the raw upstream 31-bit VariantKey REF+ALT code.

name: decode_variantkey
description: Decode a VariantKey into its raw upstream numeric fields: chrom_code, pos0, and refalt_code.

name: reverse_variantkey
description: Decode a VariantKey into a STRUCT with chrom, chrom_code, 1-based pos, upstream 0-based pos0, ref, alt, refalt_code, and reversible. For hashed nonreversible keys, reversible is FALSE and ref/alt are returned as NULL because DuckHTS v1 does not ship the optional NRVK lookup sidecar.

name: variantkey_range
description: Return the inclusive minimum and maximum VariantKey bounds for a chromosome plus 1-based VCF position range, suitable for numeric range filtering on precomputed VariantKeys.

name: regionkey
description: Encode a genomic interval as an official RegionKey-compatible 64-bit unsigned integer. Start and end use 0-based half-open interval semantics, matching BED-style coordinates; strand accepts -1, 0, or 1.

name: regionkey_hex
description: Render a RegionKey as its lowercase 16-character hexadecimal string representation.

name: parse_regionkey_hex
description: Parse a 16-character hexadecimal RegionKey string back into its UBIGINT code. Invalid or non-hex strings return NULL.

name: encode_regionkey
description: Encode the raw upstream RegionKey fields directly: chromosome code, 0-based start, 0-based end, and strand code (0 = unknown, 1 = +, 2 = -).

name: extract_regionkey_chrom
description: Extract the raw upstream RegionKey chromosome code.

name: extract_regionkey_startpos
description: Extract the raw upstream RegionKey 0-based start position.

name: extract_regionkey_endpos
description: Extract the raw upstream RegionKey 0-based end position.

name: extract_regionkey_strand
description: Extract the raw upstream RegionKey strand code (0 = unknown, 1 = +, 2 = -).

name: decode_regionkey
description: Decode a RegionKey into its raw upstream numeric fields: chrom_code, start, end, and strand_code.

name: reverse_regionkey
description: Decode a RegionKey into a STRUCT with chrom, chrom_code, start, end, strand, and strand_code.

name: extend_regionkey
description: Extend a RegionKey interval by a fixed number of bases on both sides, clamping to the official 28-bit RegionKey position range.

name: are_overlapping_regions
signature: are_overlapping_regions(chrom_a, start_a, end_a, chrom_b, start_b, end_b)
description: Return TRUE when two explicit 0-based half-open intervals overlap on the same canonical chromosome.

name: are_overlapping_region_regionkey
description: Return TRUE when a 0-based half-open interval overlaps the supplied RegionKey interval.

name: are_overlapping_regionkeys
description: Return TRUE when two RegionKeys overlap.

name: bcftools_liftover
signature: bcftools_liftover(chrom, pos, ref, alt, chain_path, dst_fasta_ref, src_fasta_ref, max_snp_gap, max_indel_inc, lift_mt, end_pos, no_left_align)
description: Row-oriented liftover kernel intended to mirror bcftools +liftover semantics as closely as possible while returning one STRUCT per input row with fields: src_chrom, src_pos, src_ref, src_alt, dest_chrom, dest_pos, dest_end, dest_ref, dest_alt, mapped, reverse_complemented, swap, reject_reason, and note. Set no_left_align := true to skip post-liftover left-alignment of lifted indels (mirrors --no-left-align in bcftools +liftover).
examples: SELECT (bcftools_liftover(chrom, pos, ref, alt, 'hg19ToHg38.over.chain.gz', 'hg38.fa', 'hg19.fa', 1, 250, false, NULL::BIGINT, false)).dest_pos FROM variants;

name: duckdb_liftover
signature: duckdb_liftover(table_name, chrom_col, pos_col, ref_col := NULL, alt_col := NULL, chain_path := NULL, dst_fasta_ref := NULL, src_fasta_ref := NULL, max_snp_gap := 1, max_indel_inc := 250, lift_mt := false, end_pos_col := NULL, no_left_align := false)
description: DuckDB-specific wrapper over bcftools_liftover that takes either a table name or a derived-table expression plus column-name strings for chrom/pos/ref/alt and returns the lifted table. The no_left_align parameter mirrors --no-left-align in bcftools +liftover.
examples: SELECT * FROM duckdb_liftover('variants', 'chrom', 'pos', ref_col := 'ref', alt_col := 'alt', chain_path := 'hg19ToHg38.over.chain.gz', dst_fasta_ref := 'hg38.fa'); || SELECT * FROM duckdb_liftover('(SELECT chrom, pos, ref, alt FROM variants) AS v', 'chrom', 'pos', ref_col := 'ref', alt_col := 'alt', chain_path := 'hg19ToHg38.over.chain.gz', dst_fasta_ref := 'hg38.fa');

name: bcftools_norm_row
signature: bcftools_norm_row(chrom, pos, ref, alt, fasta_ref, end_pos := NULL, svlen := NULL, fasta_index_path := NULL, gzi_path := NULL)
description: Normalize one variant row with bcftools/vt-style left-alignment semantics against a FASTA reference. The alt argument may be either a comma-delimited VARCHAR or a VARCHAR[] list. The returned STRUCT contains pos_normed, end_pos_normed, ref_normed, alt_normed (always VARCHAR[]), normed (TRUE/FALSE/NULL), and norm_status. Symbolic <DEL> rows can use end_pos, and symbolic <DUP> rows can use svlen.
examples: SELECT nr.pos_normed, nr.ref_normed, nr.alt_normed FROM (SELECT bcftools_norm_row('chr1', 100, 'AC', 'A', 'ref.fa', NULL::BIGINT, NULL::BIGINT, NULL, NULL) AS nr);

name: duckhts_bcftools_norm
signature: duckhts_bcftools_norm(table_name, fasta_ref, chrom_col := 'chrom', pos_col := 'pos', ref_col := 'ref', alt_col := 'alt', split_multiallelic := FALSE, end_pos_col := NULL, svlen_col := NULL, fasta_index_path := NULL, gzi_path := NULL)
description: DuckDB table macro wrapper over bcftools_norm_row that normalizes variants from a table or derived-table expression while preserving the original columns. The input ALT column may be either VARCHAR or VARCHAR[]. The result appends pos_normed, end_pos_normed, ref_normed, alt_normed, normed, and norm_status; with split_multiallelic := TRUE, multiallelic sites are split before normalization and alt_normed becomes VARCHAR plus alt_index.
examples: SELECT * FROM duckhts_bcftools_norm('variants', 'ref.fa'); || SELECT * FROM duckhts_bcftools_norm('(SELECT CHROM AS chrom, POS AS pos, REF AS ref, ALT AS alt FROM read_bcf(''cohort.vcf.gz'')) AS v', 'ref.fa', split_multiallelic := TRUE);

name: bcftools_score
signature: bcftools_score(bcf_path, summary_path_or_list, use := NULL, columns := 'PLINK', columns_file := NULL, q_score_thr := NULL, summaries_list_file := NULL, log_path := NULL, use_variant_id := FALSE, counts := FALSE, samples := NULL, force_samples := FALSE, regions := NULL, regions_file := NULL, regions_overlap := 1, targets := NULL, targets_file := NULL, targets_overlap := 0, apply_filters := NULL, include := NULL, exclude := NULL)
description: Compute polygenic scores from one genotype BCF/VCF and one or more summary-statistics files with bcftools +score-compatible GT/DS/HDS/AP/GP/AS dosage semantics, sample subsetting, and region/target/FILTER-string controls. The second argument accepts a scalar path or a DuckDB LIST/array of paths; TSV/SSF summaries produce one PRS column per file in a single genotype scan, while GWAS-VCF summaries still produce one PRS column per FORMAT sample. Use summaries_list_file with a NULL second argument to read paths from a file or directory; list-file entries are interpreted as written, matching upstream `bcftools +score --summaries` behavior, while directory inputs scan supported regular summary files in lexicographic order and ignore index sidecars. Use log_path to write per-PRS loaded/matched/allele-mismatch/duplicate-marker audit counts.
examples: SELECT * FROM bcftools_score('cohort.bcf', 'gwas.tsv.gz', columns := 'PLINK') LIMIT 5; || SELECT * FROM bcftools_score('cohort.bcf', ['score1.tsv.gz', 'score2.tsv.gz'], columns := 'GWAS-SSF') LIMIT 5; || SELECT * FROM bcftools_score('cohort.bcf', NULL, columns := 'GWAS-SSF', summaries_list_file := 'scores.list', log_path := 'score.log') LIMIT 5;

name: bcftools_munge_row
signature: bcftools_munge_row(chrom, pos, a1, a2, id, p, z, or, beta, n, n_cas, n_con, info, frq, se, lp, ac, neff, neffdiv2, het_i2, het_p, het_lp, dire, fasta_ref, iffy_tag := 'IFFY', mismatch_tag := 'REF_MISMATCH', ns := NULL, nc := NULL, ne := NULL)
description: Normalize one summary-statistics row into GWAS-VCF-style fields (chrom/pos/ref/alt/effect metrics), resolving REF/ALT orientation against a FASTA reference and applying swap-aware sign/frequency/count transforms. The output flag `alleles_swapped` means REF/ALT orientation was swapped to match the FASTA reference.
examples: SELECT (bcftools_munge_row('chr1', 12345, 'A', 'G', 'rs1', 0.01, NULL, NULL, 0.12, 1000, NULL, NULL, NULL, 0.3, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, 'ref.fa')).ref;

name: duckdb_munge
signature: duckdb_munge(table_name, preset := '', column_map := map([''], ['']), column_map_file := '', fasta_ref := NULL, iffy_tag := 'IFFY', mismatch_tag := 'REF_MISMATCH', ns := NULL, nc := NULL, ne := NULL)
description: DuckDB macro wrapper over bcftools_munge_row that maps source columns (via preset or explicit map) and returns normalized GWAS-VCF-style rows with lean outputs and explicit `alleles_swapped` semantics. Output columns: chrom, pos, id, ref, alt, alleles_swapped, filter, ns, ez, nc, es, se, lp, af, ac, ne (16 columns). For METAL meta-analysis output with SI/I2/CQ/ED columns, use duckdb_munge_metal.
examples: SELECT * FROM duckdb_munge('gwas_table', preset := 'PLINK', fasta_ref := 'ref.fa'); || SELECT * FROM duckdb_munge('(SELECT * FROM gwas_table) AS s', column_map := map(['CHR','BP','A1','A2','SNP'], ['chrom','pos','ea','nea','id']), fasta_ref := 'ref.fa');

name: duckdb_munge_metal
signature: duckdb_munge_metal(table_name, preset := '', column_map := map([''], ['']), column_map_file := '', fasta_ref := NULL, iffy_tag := 'IFFY', mismatch_tag := 'REF_MISMATCH', ns := NULL, nc := NULL, ne := NULL)
description: Extended munge macro with METAL meta-analysis output columns. Same as duckdb_munge but additionally emits: si (imputation info, from INFO input), i2 (Cochran's I² heterogeneity, from HET_I2), cq (Cochran's Q -log10 p, from HET_LP or -log10(HET_P)), and ed (effect direction string, from DIRE; +/- flipped on allele swap). The R wrapper rduckhts_munge() auto-dispatches to this macro when metal keys (INFO, HET_I2, HET_P, HET_LP, DIRE) are present in the resolved column map.
examples: SELECT * FROM duckdb_munge_metal('metal_results', preset := 'METAL', fasta_ref := 'ref.fa'); || SELECT * FROM duckdb_munge_metal('meta', column_map := map(['CHR','BP','A1','A2','SNP','HET_I2','DIRE'], ['chr','pos','ea','nea','snp','HetISq','Direction']), fasta_ref := 'ref.fa');

name: hts_union_query
r_wrapper: rduckhts_bam_multi, rduckhts_bcf_multi, rduckhts_fastq_multi, rduckhts_fasta_multi, rduckhts_bed_multi, rduckhts_tabix_multi, rduckhts_gff_multi, rduckhts_gtf_multi
description: Generate a UNION ALL BY NAME query string that reads every file matching a glob pattern through the named reader function. The result includes a 'filename' column identifying the source file for each row. Assign to a variable with SET VARIABLE and execute via query(getvariable(...)). Optional params string is appended to each reader call. In R, use the typed rduckhts_*_multi() helpers instead, which accept file vectors with optional per-file parameters and create DuckDB tables directly.
examples: SET VARIABLE q = hts_union_query('read_bam', 'samples/*.bam'); SELECT * FROM query(getvariable('q')); || SET VARIABLE q = hts_union_query('read_bcf', 'cohort/*.vcf.gz', 'tidy_format := true'); SELECT * FROM query(getvariable('q'));

name: seq_revcomp
description: Compute the reverse complement of a DNA sequence using A, C, G, T, and N bases.

name: seq_canonical
description: Return the lexicographically smaller of a sequence and its reverse complement.

name: seq_hash_2bit
description: Encode a short DNA sequence as a 2-bit unsigned integer hash.

name: seq_encode_4bit
description: Encode an IUPAC DNA sequence as a list of 4-bit base codes, preserving ambiguity symbols including N.

name: seq_decode_4bit
description: Decode a list of 4-bit IUPAC DNA base codes back into a sequence string.

name: seq_gc_content
description: Compute GC fraction for a DNA sequence as a value between 0 and 1.

name: seq_kmers
description: Expand a sequence into positional k-mers with optional canonicalization.

name: sam_flag_bits
description: Decode a SAM flag into a struct of boolean bit fields using explicit SAM-oriented names such as `is_paired`, `is_proper_pair`, `is_next_segment_unmapped`, and `is_supplementary`.

name: sam_flag_has
description: Test whether any bits from the provided SAM flag mask are set in a flag value.

name: is_forward_aligned
description: Test whether a mapped segment is aligned to the forward strand. Returns `NULL` for unmapped segments because SAM flag `0x10` does not define genomic strand when `0x4` is set.

name: cigar_has_soft_clip
description: Test whether a CIGAR string contains any soft-clipped segment (`S`).

name: cigar_has_hard_clip
description: Test whether a CIGAR string contains any hard-clipped segment (`H`).

name: cigar_left_soft_clip
description: Return the left-end soft-clipped length from a CIGAR string, or zero if the alignment does not start with `S`.

name: cigar_right_soft_clip
description: Return the right-end soft-clipped length from a CIGAR string, or zero if the alignment does not end with `S`.

name: cigar_query_length
description: Return the query-consuming length from a CIGAR string, counting `M`, `I`, `S`, `=`, and `X`.

name: cigar_aligned_query_length
description: Return the aligned query length from a CIGAR string, counting `M`, `=`, and `X` but excluding clips and insertions.

name: cigar_reference_length
description: Return the reference-consuming length from a CIGAR string, counting `M`, `D`, `N`, `=`, and `X`.

name: cigar_has_op
description: Test whether a CIGAR string contains at least one instance of the requested operator.

name: is_paired
description: Test whether the SAM flag indicates that the template has multiple segments in sequencing (`0x1`).

name: is_proper_pair
description: Test whether the SAM flag indicates that each segment is properly aligned according to the aligner (`0x2`).

name: is_unmapped
description: Test whether the read itself is unmapped according to the SAM flag.

name: is_next_segment_unmapped
description: Test whether the next segment in the template is flagged as unmapped (`0x8`).

name: is_reverse_complemented
description: Test whether `SEQ` is stored reverse complemented (`0x10`); for mapped reads this corresponds to reverse-strand alignment.

name: is_next_segment_reverse_complemented
description: Test whether `SEQ` of the next segment in the template is stored reverse complemented (`0x20`).

name: is_first_segment
description: Test whether the read is marked as the first segment in the template.

name: is_last_segment
description: Test whether the read is marked as the last segment in the template.

name: is_secondary
description: Test whether the alignment is marked as secondary.

name: is_qc_fail
description: Test whether the read failed vendor or pipeline quality checks.

name: is_duplicate
description: Test whether the alignment is flagged as a duplicate.

name: is_supplementary
description: Test whether the alignment is marked as supplementary.
